notes: D1.11 redone with a fitted held-out probe after the first frontier proved degenerate. Frontier informative (5 cuts). Stability over 5 draws showed actor_semantics redundant on only 60% of draws, so the single-draw knee would have frozen out a load-bearing field. Freeze limited to exact_identity per ADR-0007.
title: Information Guillotine on the hard corpus: held-out frontier + freeze stability

notes: NEGATIVE RESULT. DTL FAILS Stage 2 falsification criterion 1 on the long-horizon corpus: TCN 1.0000 vs DTL 0.4736 (base rate 0.333) at half the parameters. The hard corpus is SATURATED (five architectures tie at 0.9992) and cannot discriminate architectures. DTL is the best non-convolutional model on long sessions but loses decisively to convolution. Recommendation: do not build D2.6-D2.15 on this core.
title: DTL vs eight baselines on short and long-horizon corpora

notes: DTL-C reaches 1.0000, matching TCN, but ONLY with detached predictive heads (joint training scores 0.3333, a -0.67 defect that re-weighting does not fix). Ablation: max-pool is the only load-bearing component; multiscale/router/surprise show no benefit, though the corpus saturates so it cannot show one. Contradicts the 'detection emerges from prediction' thesis as implemented.
title: DTL-C convolutional redesign: detached-head fix and full component ablation

notes: Corpus removes saturation: TCN 1.0000 -> 0.5066. Components finally discriminate BOTH ways: multiscale +0.068 and maxpool +0.046 JUSTIFIED; router -0.115 and surprise -0.073 HARMFUL and removed by default per criterion 12. Best DTL-C 0.8137 vs best baseline 0.8060 at 4x params = COMPARABLE_BUT_COSTLIER, so criterion 1 still unmet on detection alone. Detached-heads finding reconfirmed on a third corpus (0.3333 joint).
title: Non-saturated ambiguous corpus: component ablation with headroom
